name: weave_run_model
description: Runs a Weave AI model directly — no Weave tool needed — and returns a prediction id; poll it with weave_get_model_run_output. Call weave_find_model first for the model `id` and its `contract`. Running spends the user's Weave credits, so it is gated: a call without `acknowledgedCost` only quotes and spends nothing, returning `inputs_required` or `cost_confirmation_required` with instructions to follow. Always show the user the cost and get an explicit Approve/Cancel (a structured prompt, not free text) before echoing `acknowledgedCost` to run — every run, including reruns. Ask the user for any input you don't have; never invent one. Running a workflow is not supported here: say so, and give its Weave editor link from weave_get_workflow. If it has a tool, offer to run the tool instead (same id) and call weave_run_tool only if the user agrees. To run it from here later, the user can create a tool from it in the editor (https://help.weavy.ai/en/articles/12267755-tools). If it has no tool, you may offer to run its models one by one with weave_run_model, saying plainly that this is not running the workflow: only its model nodes run this way, so steps like crops, compositing and exports are skipped and nothing is saved back to the workflow, so results will differ. Never say you ran the workflow.

input.description: The values to run with, keyed by the names in weave_find_model's `contract` — its `inputs` and `params` together, as one flat object. Send an array only for a field that declares `maxItems`; a field without one takes a single value. For a media input, pass the whole asset object from weave_upload_asset or a run output (or an https URL for external media).

acknowledgedCost.description: The `cost` this tool quoted in its `cost_confirmation_required` response, echoed back after the user approves, to confirm the spend and run. Omit it on the first call.
